request: how does a sundial tell the time?

beats.intent: A sundial face with hour lines from 6 am to 6 pm and a shadow at noon
beats.narration: A sundial's pointer casts a shadow on a dial marked with the hours.
beats.code:
stage.title("A sundial")
c = np.array([0, -1.8, 0])
lines = VGroup()
for h in range(6, 19):
    a = PI - (h - 6) * PI / 12
    lines.add(Line(c, c + 3.4 * np.array([np.cos(a), np.sin(a), 0]), color=GREY_B, stroke_width=2))
nums = VGroup(*[Text(str(h if h <= 12 else h - 12), font_size=22).move_to(c + 3.8 * np.array([np.cos(PI - (h - 6) * PI / 12), np.sin(PI - (h - 6) * PI / 12), 0]))
                for h in range(6, 19, 2)])
stage.play(Create(lines), FadeIn(nums))
stage.add(lines, nums)
shadow = Line(c, c + 3.2 * UP, color=ORANGE, stroke_width=8)
stage.play(Create(shadow))
stage.add(shadow)
stage.caption("noon: the shadow points straight up the dial")

beats.intent: The shadow sweeping round to 3 pm, 45° further
beats.narration: As the Sun crosses the sky the shadow turns, fifteen degrees every hour. Three hours later it points at three.
beats.code:
stage.play(Rotate(shadow, -PI / 4, about_point=c), run_time=2)
stage.caption("3 pm: turned 3 × 15° = 45°")

beats.intent: The dial beside 360° ÷ 24 h = 15° per hour
beats.narration: The Earth turns once in twenty four hours: three hundred and sixty degrees, fifteen each hour.

request: how can a steel ship float when steel sinks?

beats.intent: A solid steel block sinking to the bottom of a tank
beats.narration: A lump of steel sinks: it is about eight times as dense as water.
beats.code:
stage.title("Why ships float")
tank = Rectangle(width=10, height=3.2, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.2).move_to([0, -1.5, 0])
stage.play(FadeIn(tank))
stage.add(tank)
block = Square(0.7, color=GREY_B, fill_opacity=0.9).move_to([-3, 1.2, 0])
stage.play(FadeIn(block))
stage.play(block.animate.move_to([-3, -2.75, 0]), run_time=1.2)
stage.add(block)
stage.label(block, "steel lump", direction=UP)

beats.intent: The same steel shaped into a wide open hull floating, sitting low in the water
beats.narration: Shape the same steel into a wide, hollow hull. Now it pushes a lot of water aside as it settles.
beats.code:
surf = tank.get_top()[1]
hull = Polygon([1.0, surf + 0.5, 0], [4.0, surf + 0.5, 0], [3.6, surf - 0.5, 0], [1.4, surf - 0.5, 0], color=GREY_B, fill_opacity=0.3, stroke_width=6)
stage.play(Create(hull))
stage.add(hull)
under = Polygon([1.0 + 0.2, surf, 0], [4.0 - 0.2, surf, 0], [3.6, surf - 0.5, 0], [1.4, surf - 0.5, 0], stroke_width=0, fill_color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.6)
stage.play(FadeIn(under))
stage.add(under)
stage.label(under, "water pushed aside", direction=DOWN, color=BLUE)

beats.intent: Bars: weight of the ship equal to the weight of water pushed aside
beats.narration: It floats when the water it pushes aside weighs as much as the whole ship. The water pushes back up with exactly that force.
beats.code:
stage.clear()
b = draw_bars(stage, [10, 10], labels=["ship's weight", "water displaced"], color=TEAL)
stage.caption("floating: the two weights match")

request: how do you split a £90 bill when one person had twice as much?

beats.intent: A bar for £90 split into 4 equal parts of £22.50
beats.narration: Three friends share a ninety pound bill, but one had twice as much. Count shares: one, one and two, four in all.
beats.code:
stage.title("Splitting a bill")
parts = VGroup(*[Rectangle(width=2.2, height=0.9, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.5, fill_color=c) for c in (BLUE, GREEN, ORANGE, ORANGE)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0).move_to([0, 0.5, 0])
stage.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(p) for p in parts], lag_ratio=0.2))
stage.add(parts)
stage.label(parts, "£90", direction=UP)
for p in parts:
    t = Text("£22.50", font_size=24).move_to(p)
    stage.add(t)
    stage.play(FadeIn(t), run_time=0.2)

beats.intent: The shares grouped by person: Ana £22.50, Ben £22.50, Cal £45
beats.narration: Each share is ninety over four: twenty two fifty. Ana and Ben pay one share each; Cal pays two, forty five pounds.
beats.code:
for grp, name, col in ((parts[0:1], "Ana £22.50", BLUE), (parts[1:2], "Ben £22.50", GREEN), (parts[2:4], "Cal £45", ORANGE)):
    br = Brace(VGroup(*grp), DOWN, color=col)
    stage.play(GrowFromCenter(br), run_time=0.4)
    stage.add(br)
    stage.label(br, name, direction=DOWN, color=col)

beats.narration: Total divided by the number of shares gives one share; multiply by each person's shares.

request: with 20 m of fence, what rectangle gives the biggest area?

beats.intent: Three rectangles with perimeter 20: 8 by 2, 6 by 4, 5 by 5, with their areas
beats.narration: Twenty metres of fence can make many rectangles: eight by two, six by four, five by five.
beats.code:
stage.title("Most area from 20 m of fence")
k = 0.42
rects = VGroup(*[Rectangle(width=w * k, height=h * k, color=c, fill_opacity=0.35) for w, h, c in ((8, 2, BLUE), (6, 4, GREEN), (5, 5, ORANGE))])
rects.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.8, aligned_edge=DOWN).move_to([0, 0, 0])
stage.play(LaggedStart(*[Create(r) for r in rects], lag_ratio=0.3))
stage.add(rects)
for r, t in zip(rects, ["8×2 = 16", "6×4 = 24", "5×5 = 25"]):
    stage.label(r, t + " m²", direction=DOWN, color=r.get_color())

beats.intent: Axes of width and area with the curve A = w(10 - w), peaking at w = 5
beats.narration: Width w leaves ten minus w for the other side, so the area is w times ten minus w. It peaks in the middle.
beats.code:
stage.clear()
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(0, 10), y_range=(0, 30), labels=("width", "area"))
g = plot_graph(stage, ax, lambda w: w * (10 - w), color=ORANGE)
top = mark_point(stage, ax, (5, 25), color=YELLOW, label="(5, 25)")

beats.intent: The curve beside A = w(10 - w), largest at w = 5: a square
beats.narration: The best rectangle is a square, five by five: twenty five square metres.
